title: A LIVE worker thread blocked inside the queue critical section for more than the 60 s thread lease is displaced like a dead one and can then clobber the displacer's write after its last check
evidence: Threads share the pid, so a terminated worker and one blocked inside the critical section look identical from outside; the lease (hold time >= 60 s for a holder whose recorded thread id is > 0) is the bound that ends the up-to-1 h outage of ISS-JOBQSTALL-002. Pinned by the unit test 'a holder displaced as a reused pid / expired lease while it is mid-operation': the displaced worker gets conflict at its token + content re-check. The window that remains is the same as ISS-JOBQSTALL-001: displaced AFTER its last check, at the rename, it still overwrites. Needs a live worker thread stalled >60 s inside a millisecond critical section (hung network fs, debugger pause); the main thread is exempt (keeps the 1 h protection).
fix_direction: None cheap: a rename cannot compare-and-swap. Either wire the queue so callers treat conflict as retry-with-alert and keep the lease, or raise the lease; a heartbeat does not help (the critical section is synchronous, no timer can run in it).
class: data write, narrow window, no known trigger

title: Pid-reuse detection is best-effort: it needs the OS start time and a lock at least staleMs (30 s) old; otherwise the old 1 h rule applies
evidence: (a) Start time unavailable (Windows: Get-Process denied for a process of another user or an elevated one; PowerShell missing or slower than the 5 s timeout; macOS ps failure; Linux CLK_TCK not 100) -> null -> unknown -> the pid-only rule (conflict up to 1 h). (b) A reused pid whose process started within 1 s of the lock being written is not recognised (slack). (c) A lock younger than 30 s is never judged by identity, so for the first 30 s after a holder died and its pid was reused writers get conflict. (d) A wall-clock step backwards by more than the holder's age between its process start and its lock write could make a genuine, stalled holder look reused (needs a stall >= 30 s as well). (e) The Windows lookup blocks the caller ~0.3-0.5 s once per call, only for a lock >= 30 s old.
fix_direction: Accept as documented; or record the holder's own start time in the lock body at acquire (free for its own pid) and compare equality instead of start > at, which removes (b) and (d).
class: availability of data write path, no loss
